name: Visitor eVisa

requirements.blocker_text: Any holder of a valid passport wishing to enter Montserrat as a visitor or on business may apply; the passport must remain valid for the duration of the trip.

evidence_required.document: Online eVisa application with passport and payment details
Combined application/processing fee: US$50 (credit card only), non-refundable
Invitation letter or supporting documents, if requested

outcome.duration_length: not fixed on the eVisa itself; the Immigration Act (Section 18) caps visitor/temporary admission at 6 months, extendable by the Chief Immigration Officer to a maximum of 12 months

sources.title: Government of Montserrat -- Online Immigration & Customs Portal: Tourist eVisa guide, eligibility, fee (US$50), 24-hour processing
Montserrat Chapter 13.01, Immigration Act -- Section 18 (visitor/temporary admission periods), Section 18 OECS-citizen automatic 6-month provision

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Montserrat's initial build (first British Overseas Territory built after Anguilla -- see ms_belonger_status_descent.json's notes for the same BOT-vs-citizenship framing decision applied throughout this country's routes). The eVisa portal (immigration.ms) governs the online application step; the underlying legal duration/extension framework comes from the Immigration Act Section 18, which also grants citizens of Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States (OECS) member countries automatic 6-month residence rights on arrival, not modelled as a separate route since it is a nationality-based exemption within this same visitor framework rather than a distinct application. Whether every nationality can use the eVisa or must instead apply via embassy/consulate was not independently confirmed at tier-1 in this pass -- the source states some nationalities require a visa and refers applicants to a country-specific list not reviewed here.
